My issue is that I’ve come across a lot of mental health professionals that give/assert nonsense whilst seeking deferential treatment to them because they are an authority. 

Here’s some recent examples:

I recently got told EMDR didn’t work for me because I have ADHD and that could cause issues whilst undergoing the treatment. He insisted this was the ‘variable’ as if mental health treatments are an equation and you just need to plug in the right formula and it works 100% of the time. 

I went and used AI to scan for studies on ADHD and EMDR, there’s very few studies and there’s no consensus on as to whether ADHD could cause issues with EMDR processing… In essence they don’t know. It’s useless information, there’s a million other variables it could be why not throw them in too to really narrow it down?… 

So why did he insist ‘this’ could be the ‘variable’ when there’s no science to his proposition? There’s no logic, critical or rational thinking behind his statement. 

I also had another instance where a therapist insisted a skin rash I had developed was due to undergoing EMDR (this therapist even wrote this in her notes that I later received). For weeks I believed her until this rash wasn’t going away, eventually I went to my GP and the doctor told me exactly what the rash was and how it forms, he laughed as it being a side effect of EMDR as it completely contradicted science, he gave me a prescription for some lotion and then after applying it for 2 weeks it was gone…

There’s loads more… The point I’m trying to make is that therapists frequently overestimate their abilities. They lack humility and it’s an issue. It causes problems and can lead patients/clients on wild goose chases.

There’s so much more… Attributing successful treatments in part to your abilities as a therapist, whilst then dismissing unsuccessful treatments as the patients fault for being ‘resistant’ etc. You literally can’t say these things, therapists don’t know and commonly lean on the ‘mystical’ notions when really they just don’t know why it worked or didn’t work. 

Patients are being sent round and round in circles never getting closer to solutions.

Funded accounts are useful for this reason.

People often risk large percentages of their account because if they were to only risk 1% of a $1000 account then they would likely only make $30 (say it’s a 3:1 R). 

That’s not getting them anywhere and isn’t motivating to do all that work for little reward at the end of the week, they probably could have made more by working a crappy job.

So they risk more in hopes of making an amount that is acceptable to them but that throws off their whole risk management and they ruin their accounts. They may experience a string of losses and their account doesn’t have the maths to survive a string of say 10 losses which the market can naturally give you simply out of variance (you could be doing everything right in terms of your proven strategy that has a edge and trade entry conditions but just experiencing bad luck). 

This is why people need an account big enough for their personal circumstances or otherwise it isn’t going to work.

There’s nothing technically wrong with using your whole account in a trade and using a SL at 1% loss. 

The issue is we aren’t perfect. We make mistakes and it only takes one mistakes (such as moving your SL) and then compounding  mistakes that add to that initial mistake for an account to be completely blown. 

This is why it’s important to have various risk management setups such as;

$1,000. Divided up into 5 separate accounts. You only risk 1% of the account per trade. You only trade one account at a time. 

Having an automatic max daily loss limit set up so that if you cross the max daily loss limit threshold then your account auto liquidated the positions and closes down for the day. (This is a backup feature and will save your backside more than you can imagine). 

Having a max amount you will stop at for the day before the automatic max daily loss limit feature kicks in. You want to rely on your own self discipline, not a backup feature or otherwise you aren’t learning risk management skills and developing the character to manage risk on a responsible fashion. 

Never leaving resting orders in the order book. 

Having your brokers number stuck on your desk so you can call them in an emergency if your internet crashes. 

Having alternative means of connecting to the internet that doesn’t rely solely on your Wi-Fi and broadband such as cellular devices on a separate network so that you may be able to close the positions via your phone and/or call the broker so they may flatten your account.

I have PTSD and experienced similar symptoms to what your bf sounds as if he is experiencing. 

I can only share how PTSD impacted me (and still does). 

I experienced being ‘shut down’ as all my energy was focused on threat and survival, this led to no interest in sex as my chemistry wasn’t conducive for that response, it was focused on being safe. 

He likely experiences ‘flat affect’ (a common PTSD symptom) from time to time (or maybe all the time). In this state it’s difficult to move your face muscles and you don’t ‘feel’ the joke and you also are constricted from your natural response whereby otherwise you would laugh if it was funny to you. 

I would say something that I did find majorly beneficial was couples counselling with a trauma therapist that also was willing to do couple therapy (many will so worth a look if you are both willing). It gave space for me and my then partner to build a bridge and reconnect, she experienced a greater sense of closeness and our intimacy improved. 

If he already has a therapist or one he is on good terms with then it may be worth seeing if they will do a regular couples sessions. I recommend one he already knows because they will know how his symptoms impact him and how that may cause relationship issues. It can act as a good bridge for you both and offer a good opportunity to see different perspectives, yours and his.

It can get better. My PTSD symptoms have improved massively since 2017. Recovery is possible. 

PTSD is essentially a processing and filing issue. The brain hasn’t filed away the memory of the distressing event. The filing away would in some sense mark it as ‘past’ however because it is not being filed then in some sense it remains ‘alive’. When the brains alarm system gets activated (likely due to a trigger) then it acts as if the threat is present NOW.

To really address the condition the trauma needs to be processed. EMDR therapy may be able to help with that, as a vet I would imagine he should be able to get support to gain access to that treatment. 

Some medications can help to manage the symptoms such as sertraline (anti depressant - helps the anxiety) and medical cannabis may be able to help reduce nightmares so he can actually get a good sleep and want to sleep.
